page: Amazon Web Services r6gd.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the 64-bit Arm Neoverse-N1 architecture running on the AWS Nitro System. The instance provides 4 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core clocked at 2.5 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields an 8.0 GB per-core allocation ratio. Hardware features include an L1 data cache of 64 KB, an L2 cache of 1.0 MB, and an L3 cache of 32 MB, alongside hardware-accelerated AES cryptography. The instance includes a bundled 237 GB local NVMe SSD instance storage volume and a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight mixed performance characteristics across compute and memory workloads. In memory bandwidth testing, large block uncached reads and writes reached 71.58 GB/sec and 34.94 GB/sec respectively, placing in the average benchmark category. PassMark database operations scored 2599.67, also performing in the middle tier. In contrast, pure compute throughput ranks in lower brackets: stress-ng single-core scored 1519.59 while multi-core reached 6052.47. PassMark CPU overall reached 2690.0 and Geekbench single-core and multi-core scored 957.0 and 3208.0, indicating modest raw compute compared to high-frequency x86 alternatives.

The primary tradeoff of the r6gd.xlarge lies in its emphasis on high memory density and high-speed local NVMe storage over raw computing power and network throughput. It provides an efficient resource footprint for memory-bound applications that require low-latency scratch space or temporary operational stores. It is well-suited for distributed caching tiers, in-memory databases, batch database processing, and lightweight data staging pipelines that do not depend on high baseline networking or intense mathematical processing.
description: Amazon Web Services r6gd.xlarge is an Arm-based memory-optimized instance featuring 4 dedicated physical cores on the Neoverse-N1 architecture clocked at 2.5 GHz. Configured on the Nitro hypervisor, it supplies 32.0 GB of RAM, offering a high 8.0 GB per-core memory ratio. The server includes 237 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a baseline network interface of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations show solid database operations and large-block memory bandwidth, with PassMark database operations scoring 2599.67 and memory write bandwidth reaching 34.94 GB/sec. Pure computational metrics show moderate performance, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 3208.0 and PassMark CPU score of 2690.0. The r6gd.xlarge represents an efficient deployment target for memory-intensive workloads requiring rapid local scratch space, such as Redis caches, relational database read replicas, and real-time data ingestion pipelines.
